/Education
We know that environmental challenges aren’t solved by science alone—they’re solved by people. That’s why we’re dedicated to educating the next generation of environmental problem-solvers with both a strong scientific foundation and a deep understanding of the societal context. It’s this combination that gives students the tools they need to take action and create real change.
Search among all our courses and programmes
The Department of Environmental Science offers education at all levels, including a Bachelor’s programme, four Master’s programmes, and a PhD programme. Our Master’s programmes allow you to deepen your expertise within your chosen field — explore the articles below to learn more.
Most courses welcome students from other departments, provided the entry requirements are met, and some courses are even open to the public.
Ready to apply? Step-by-step guide to application
In a 2024 survey of Environmental Science Master’s students, 15 out of 16 respondents said that the program met or exceeded their expectations. 75% of respondents selected ACES/Stockholm University due to its strong research reputation.
Read more about our research projects
Bachelor's programme in Environmental Science (in Swedish)
Students sampling at Askö field station. Photo: Michaela Lundell
The bachelor’s programme in Environmental Science focuses on identifying, understanding and resolving different environmental challenges, like global warming, chemicals in the environment and reduced biodiversity. You begin with a broad introduction that focuses on understanding a number of scientific disciplines required for working with environmental issues. The second year allows you to chose your specialisation – biology, earth sciences or chemistry.
Bachelor's Programme in Environmental Science
Master's programme - Atmosphere, Biogeochemistry and Climate
This is the broadest programme, focusing on how large-scale systems interact, on how human perturbations upset these balances; and on potential solutions to these problems.
Master's Programme in Environmental Science - Atmosphere, Biogeochemistry and Climate
Master's programme - Environmental Toxicology and Chemistry
This programme looks at the chemical and physical properties of contaminants, the ways that they impact the environment and the regulatory systems built to control them.
Master's Programme in Environmental Science - Environmental Toxicology and Chemistry
Master's programme - Transdisciplinary Studies of Climate, Environment, and Energy
The Master's Programme in Transdisciplinary Studies of Climate, Environment, and Energy (TRACEE) offered by the CIVIS European University Alliance, equips you with the knowledge to understand the complex problems of climate, energy, and environmental systems and provides you with the tools to create solutions from natural science, society and human perspectives, through what we call a transdisciplinary approach.
Master's Programme in Transdisciplinary Studies of Climate, Environment and Energy
Master's programme - Environmental Health Protection
The programme, Environmental Health Protection (offered only in Swedish), brings together environmental science and societal impact, and is a highly desirable credential for employers in the public and private sectors.
Master's Programme in Environment and Health Protection (in Swedish)
Course package in Environment and Health
Combine full-time studies with part-time work in our unique one-year work-integrated program in Environment and Health. Gain in-demand skills through case studies, theory, and hands-on experience. Work up to 15 hours per week alongside your studies, applying your knowledge in a real-world setting. This program prepares you for careers as an environmental consultant, sustainability officer, or health inspector—meeting the strong demand for expertise in sustainability and environmental management.

PhD studies
The department offers a PhD programme in Environmental Science, generally four years fulltime, which includes course work and a research project supervised by one of our researchers. Positions are limited and are announced four times per year (April, June, October and December) on our website.
